subject: Intermittent 503s + latency spike on Reserved GPU pool — immediate update and next steps

Date: 2026-11-20T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: High error rate and latency on reserved pool this morning

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a spike in 503 errors and tail latency for our checkout-generation route around 07:45 PT this morning. Impacted requests returned 503 or timed out; our telemetry shows p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to >2s and error rate hit ~6% for ~20 minutes. We’re on a Reserved GPU pool (rsv-us-west-2-b) and this is affecting checkout traffic for US customers.

Can you confirm whether this is on your side (scheduled ops, autoscaler, or something else)? We raised an internal pager but wanted to loop you in. We rely on the reserved pool for predictable throughput — this is causing cart abandonment.

Example trace id: b3f9c1e6

Thanks,

Subject: Reserved pool hot-path eviction loop — findings and immediate mitigations

Team — quick post from the ops lane after the first look:

What we saw
- At 07:46 PT we observed a sudden increase in small, high-QPS inference requests to BrightCart’s checkout route. The workload had a high proportion of short prompt lengths which stressed the batcher hot-path.
- The batcher attempted aggressive re-packing which triggered a KV-cache eviction cascade on several nodes; that caused increased CPU/GPU context switches and momentary loss of heartbeats for a subset of replicas.
- The autoscaler responded by trying to allocate additional nodes but hit a reserved-pool allocation delay due to a transient scheduler contention window (approx 90s).

Immediate mitigations applied (07:52–08:06 PT)
- We rerouted BrightCart traffic off rsv-us-west-2-b to the warm-standby pool (rsv-us-west-2-standby) and enabled an emergency shedder for the checkout route to cap concurrency per-client.
- We disabled aggressive re-packing heuristics for the next 30 minutes to avoid repeated eviction cycles.
- We adjusted request-level batching thresholds for BrightCart to prefer smaller max batch size for short prompts.

Customer impact
- Errors fell from 6% → 0.2% within 8 minutes of routing change. Tail latency returned to baseline within ~14 minutes.

Next steps
- Postmortem write-up (DR draft) in 48 hours.
- Follow-up with credit recommendation and configuration change proposal for BrightCart (persistent per-customer concurrency cap + tailored batching profile).

I’ll prepare a short incident timeline for Karthik to send externally.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High error rate and latency on reserved pool this morning

Elaine — short update and apology for the disruption.

What happened (short)
- We observed a transient eviction loop in rsv-us-west-2-b triggered by an unusual burst of short, high-concurrency requests to your checkout-generation route. That led to momentary replica disruptions and a brief autoscaler allocation delay.

What we did
- Rerouted your traffic to warm-standby and applied per-route concurrency caps to reduce error rate.
- Tuned batching and disabled aggressive re-packing heuristics to avoid repeated KV cache churn.

Impact and status
- Error rate dropped to baseline; p95 latency back to expected levels. No data leakage.

Follow-ups we’re committing to
- Draft postmortem delivered in 48 hours for review.
- A proposed config change (persistent per-customer concurrency caps + an optimized batching profile) + recommended SLA credit for the incident window.
- A technical review call (30 min) with your SREs and our infra leads — proposed Thursday 11/25 10:00 PT. Please let me know if that slot works.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We’ll follow with the postmortem and recommended config changes.

Best,
Karthik
